This is the Tessel repo (a Flask-style framework), and the class-based view path is in `src/tessel/views.py` and `src/tessel/sansio/app.py`.

1. **Define the class.** The user subclasses `VerbView` (`src/tessel/views.py:138`) and writes `get()` and/or `post()` methods. The docstring example at `views.py:152-158` shows `CounterAPI` with both.

2. **Derive the allowed methods.** `VerbView.__init_subclass__` (`views.py:165-180`) scans the class for methods named after HTTP verbs (`http_method_funcs`, `views.py:11`) and sets `cls.methods` to the uppercased names, e.g. `{"GET", "POST"}`. It also merges in methods from base classes.

3. **Turn the class into a view function.** `View.to_view_func(name)` (`views.py:86-135`) is a classmethod. It returns a plain function `view(**kwargs)` that creates an instance of the class (or reuses one if `init_every_request` is False) and calls `self.run_view(**kwargs)`. It copies `methods` onto the function (`views.py:133`), along with the class and the decorators.

4. **Register the route.** `attach_route_rule` in `src/tessel/sansio/app.py:606` reads `view_func.methods` when no `methods=` is passed (`app.py:622-623`, default `("GET",)`). It then registers the URL rule with those methods.

5. **Dispatch per request.** `VerbView.run_view` (`views.py:182-191`) does `getattr(self, request.method.lower())`, so a `POST` calls `post()` and a `GET` calls `get()`. If a `HEAD` request has no `head()` method, it falls back to `get()`. An assertion fires if no handler exists.

The plain `View` class (`views.py:16`) skips the verb dispatch. The user overrides `run_view()` directly and the framework calls it for every allowed method.
